findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted profile field hiding
findings.body: The serializer hides `website` for restricted viewers by including it in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), but the new `website_name` attribute is derived from the same stored website and is not covered by that restriction. The inclusion hook added here also does not call `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, so for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, `website` can be omitted while `website_name` such as `example.com/path` is still serialized, leaking the profile website/path and defeating the existing privacy control.

findings.title: include_website_name is not a predicate method
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer decides whether to serialize an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. The method here is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so it is not used by the serializer. As a result, `website_name` is always serialized even for users with no website, including `website_name: nil`, and the `website.present?` guard is dead code. The method should be renamed `include_website_name?` and covered with a no-website test.

findings.title: Domain comparison treats public-suffix siblings as the same domain
findings.body: The second branch compares all but the first DNS label, which misclassifies unrelated domains sharing a multi-label public suffix. For example, with `website_host = 'evil.co.uk'` and `discourse_host = 'example.co.uk'`, both have the same label count and the comparison drops the first label to match on `co.uk`, so the serializer returns `evil.co.uk/path` even though the website domain is neither the instance domain nor a parent/subdomain of it. A proper registrable-domain/public-suffix comparison is needed to avoid showing paths for unrelated sites.
